    25 seconds later.
  - You run it yourself by typing ! sleep 25 && echo slept at the prompt. That runs it directly in this session.

  · Notes   ─────────────────────────────────────
  - The block exists so the agent doesn't sit idle on fixed waits. When the goal is to wait for a condition, a polling
    loop (until <check>; do sleep 2; done) or a background job is the recommended approach.
  - && only runs echo slept if sleep exits successfully (status 0), so stopping the sleep early with Ctrl-C would also
    skip the echo.
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
